transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess... I'm here because for the past year I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. Which, I know what I'm looking at because I'm a phlebotomist. I draw blood all day. Actually, just yesterday I had this guy come in, and his veins were just rolling everywhere, took me three tries with a butterfly needle just to get a decent draw. I felt awful, but he was so nice about it, he was telling me all about his grandson's little league game... 

But anyway, with my dad, no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know what I saw. The chart doesn’t match what I originally looked at. My sister keeps telling me to drop it, but she doesn't even work in medical, she sells insurance. Mostly auto, but she was telling me about this new boat policy she's pushing, which makes no sense since we don't even live near a lake or anything... but yeah, I just know the chart is wrong and trying to get people to listen to me is honestly just wearing me down.
Do you think someone is intentionally changing your dad's lab results?

Yes, exactly. I know they are. You don't just accidentally alter a chart or hold back specific values like that. Someone in the system is doing it on purpose. Like I was saying, I know what I saw originally, and the current chart just doesn't match. It's completely intentional. 

Which reminds me, at my clinic, we just got this new computer system update, and the screen is so incredibly bright now. My coworker, Sarah, she actually bought these blue-light blocking glasses online to deal with it. They have these really cute, thick tortoiseshell frames, but she complains they pinch right behind her ears and give her a headache. I keep telling her to just run the plastic under warm water and gently bend the arms out—my mom taught me that trick with cheap sunglasses when we went to Florida a few years ago. The humidity there was just awful, my hair was frizzy the entire trip... 

But anyway, yeah, I know someone is intentionally changing his numbers. And trying to prove it when all the doctors and my family keep telling me I'm wrong and that the results are fine... it's just really wearing me down.
Do you think someone is watching you or following you outside of the clinic?

No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed anyone following me or watching me, no. I mostly just go straight from work to home anyway. Though, my commute has been a complete nightmare lately because they're doing all that construction on the highway. They have two lanes closed down, and the traffic just backs up for miles. Yesterday, I was stuck for forty minutes behind this huge semi-truck that was hauling... I think it was frozen chickens? The logo on the back had this cartoon rooster wearing a little chef's hat, which is honestly kind of morbid if you really think about it. It's like, why is the chicken happy about cooking other chickens? 

My friend Jessica said the exact same thing when we went to this barbecue place last weekend for her birthday. She got the pulled pork, but they put way too much vinegar in the sauce. I always prefer a sweeter sauce, like a brown sugar or honey barbecue, you know? It just coats the meat better and doesn't give you that weird heartburn. She ended up not even finishing it and we just went and got ice cream instead... 

But um... wait, what were we just talking about? Oh, following me. No, nobody is watching me on the street or anything like that. It's just the people inside the medical system who are messing with my dad's chart, that's the only thing going on.
For how long have you been certain that someone is intentionally changing your dad's lab results?

Well, it's been about a year now. It all started right around the time my dad's medical issues got worse and he had to start getting all these frequent labs and appointments. Which, honestly, trying to coordinate all those appointments has been a second full-time job. The scheduling department at that main hospital is just impossible. I was on hold with them for forty-five minutes last Tuesday, and they play this awful, repetitive jazz music while you wait. It’s like a saxophone on a loop, and it sounds like it was recorded underwater. 

It reminded me of this time my high school band went to play at a competition in Chicago. We took this huge charter bus, and the AC broke down halfway there. It was May, but it was unseasonably hot, like ninety degrees, and the windows wouldn't even open. Everyone was sweating through their uniforms, and my friend Megan actually passed out in the aisle. The chaperones had to fan her with sheet music and give her all the tiny water bottles from the cooler up front. We didn't even place in the competition because half the brass section was too dehydrated to play properly. 

But yeah, ever since those frequent labs started about a year ago, that's when I noticed the numbers being changed. It's been a whole year of this.
Do you think anything else in your life is being controlled or manipulated by others?

No, no, it's really just his charts. I don't feel like the rest of my life is being manipulated or anything like that. 

Well, I mean, unless you count my landlord controlling the thermostat in my building. He put this clear plastic lock box over the dial in the hallway so none of the tenants can touch it, which is just ridiculous because it gets freezing in my unit. I actually had to go to Target on Sunday to buy a space heater. I got this little oscillating ceramic one, it was on clearance, but the second I plugged it into the wall in my bedroom, it completely blew a fuse. Half the apartment just went pitch black. I had to use the flashlight on my phone to find the breaker box, which for some reason is hidden behind this really hideous floral wallpaper inside the hall closet. 

I honestly don't know who picked out that wallpaper, it looks like it’s straight out of the 1970s. It’s all these giant mustard yellow and avocado green flowers. My aunt actually had a velvet couch in that exact same green color when I was growing up. We used to sit on it and eat those freeze pops in the summer, you know, the ones in the little plastic sleeves? The blue raspberry ones were the best, but they always stained your tongue blue for days, and my mom would get so mad if we dripped any on the carpet... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, manipulated. No, nobody is controlling my life. It's just the people in the hospital system messing with my dad's numbers. Everything else is fine.
Do you think there's anything else in your life or the world that doesn't seem quite right or isn't what it appears to be?

No, I don't think so. Everything else is pretty normal, really. Just the hospital stuff. I mean, my job at the clinic is totally fine. I draw blood all day, which you'd think would be stressful, but it's actually pretty routine once you get the hang of it. You just have to find the vein, you know? Some people have really great veins, they just pop right up. 

But then you get the people who are super dehydrated, and it's like digging for buried treasure. I had this one guy last week, he was maybe in his sixties, and he told me he only drinks black coffee and Diet Coke. No water at all. Which is so bad for your kidneys! My cousin's husband had kidney stones a few years ago, and he said it was the worst pain of his entire life. He actually had to go to the ER in the middle of the night on Christmas Eve. They were supposed to host the whole family for Christmas dinner the next day, and my cousin had already bought this massive spiral ham. She ended up having to cook it anyway because it wouldn't fit in the freezer, and she said they ate ham sandwiches for like three weeks straight. I can't even look at a ham sandwich anymore without feeling a little sick... 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, things not seeming right. No, it's just the charts. Everything else in the world is just regular stuff.
Do you think you're thinking clearly about your dad's lab results?

Of course I'm thinking clearly about them. I mean, I look at lab results all day for my job, so I know exactly what I'm looking at when I see his charts. I'm probably the only one in the family who actually understands how all the reference ranges work. 

Though our system at the clinic is actually getting updated next month, which everyone is dreading because the last time they updated the software, the main printer in the reception area just completely stopped talking to the computers. It's this massive industrial printer, one of those ones that sorts and staples everything for you. But it jammed constantly after the update. We had to call the IT guy, Kevin, like three times a week. 

Kevin is super nice, though. He actually brings his dog to work sometimes on Fridays. It's this huge golden retriever named Barnaby. Barnaby is adorable, but he sheds everywhere. I have no idea how Kevin deals with it at home. I used to have a cat, a little orange tabby, and even that was too much hair for me. I was constantly buying those sticky lint rollers in bulk from Costco. Have you ever been to Costco on a Saturday morning? It is an absolute nightmare. People will literally run you over with their oversized carts just to get a tiny paper cup with a free sample of a frozen taquito. I actually saw two grown women get into a shouting match in the bakery aisle over the last pack of blueberry muffins once. 

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, about being clear-headed. Yeah, no, I'm completely clear-headed about it. I know exactly what I'm seeing on his paperwork, and someone is definitely changing the numbers.
Do you think it's possible that you might be misremembering what you saw on your dad's original lab results?

No, absolutely not. I am not misremembering. I know what I saw. I'm here because for the past year I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his lab results. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. It's just wearing me down, honestly. 

It’s like when you know you bought a specific brand of something at the grocery store, but then you get home and it’s the store brand. My mom does that all the time. She’ll swear she bought the name-brand paper towels, the ones that are supposed to be super absorbent, but then you go to clean up a spill and it just smears it around. We had this huge spill last Thanksgiving when my uncle knocked over a whole boat of gravy. It went all over the good tablecloth, the lace one that my grandmother brought over from Ireland. My mom was so upset, she tried using club soda and salt to get the stain out, but it just made this weird crusty spot. 

She ended up having to take it to the dry cleaner down on 4th Street. The guy who runs it, Mr. Henderson, he’s been there forever. He always gives out those little hard strawberry candies with the wrappers that look like actual strawberries. I loved those when I was a kid. But anyway, he got the stain out, which was a miracle. 

But yeah, what were you asking? Oh, misremembering. No, I'm not misremembering. I know exactly what the original numbers were, and someone is definitely messing with them.
Do you think you might be overestimating the importance of these lab results or the conspiracy surrounding them?

Overestimating? No, how could I be overestimating it? Like I was just saying, I've spent this entire last year trying to expose this. Someone in that system is intentionally altering or hiding parts of my dad's results. Everyone—the doctors, my own family—keeps telling me I'm making a big deal out of nothing and that his numbers are perfectly fine. But I know the charts don't match what I originally saw, and fighting everyone on this is just completely wearing me down. 

I mean, I'm so exhausted lately I actually thought maybe it was my mattress making me tired, so I went to that big furniture store on Route 9 last weekend. The salesman there was so incredibly pushy, you know the type? He kept trying to sell me this adjustable base that costs like two thousand dollars. Like I need my bed to fold me in half like a taco. My friend Sarah bought one of those, and the remote got lost in the blankets, and she accidentally raised the foot of the bed in the middle of the night and it scared her cat so badly it scratched her leg. She had to put Neosporin on it for a week. Neosporin always smells so weird to me, kind of like petroleum jelly but medicinal. I prefer the cream kind, but the ointment is supposedly better for scarring. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Overestimating? No, it's not an overestimation. It's a massive deal. They are changing his charts, and I won't stop until I prove it, no matter how tired I am.
Do you ever have any doubts about your theory that someone is changing your dad's lab results?

Doubts? No. Why would I have doubts? I just told you, for a whole year now I have been trying to prove that someone in the clinic's system is changing his lab results, or holding parts of them back. I don't have doubts because I know what I saw. It doesn't matter that literally every doctor and my entire family keeps telling me his numbers are fine. They don't see what I see. The chart doesn't match, and it's just... it's wearing me down. 

It’s like trying to argue with a brick wall. Have you ever tried to take down a brick wall? My neighbor, Mr. Peterson, tried to take down this old brick retaining wall in his backyard last summer. He thought he could just do it himself with a sledgehammer to save money instead of hiring a contractor. He was out there for three days straight in the blistering heat, just whacking away at it. He ended up pulling a muscle in his back so badly he had to wear one of those thick black support belts for a month. He looked like a weightlifter every time he came out to get his mail. 

He gets a lot of mail, actually. Mostly those glossy catalogs for gardening supplies. He grows these massive prize-winning tomatoes. He gave me one once, and it was so big I had to slice it like a steak. I made a BLT with it, but I used turkey bacon because regular bacon has too much grease. I hate when you cook bacon and the grease splatters all over the stove and you have to scrub it with that heavy-duty degreaser that smells like fake lemons. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Doubts? Right. No, no doubts. I know they're changing the numbers, and I'm not going to stop trying to prove it, even if it's completely exhausting me.
Do you think events or things you see in your daily life are somehow related to your dad's lab results or the people changing them?

Related? No, I don't... I mean, I don't think random things in my day are connected to the clinic or the people changing the results. I'm just focused on the charts themselves, trying to get someone to see that they don't match what I originally saw. That's what's wearing me down. 

Although, speaking of daily life, I did have to get my car inspected yesterday, and that was an ordeal. I went to this place on 5th Avenue, and the mechanic told me I needed four new tires to pass. Four! I just bought two new ones last winter when we had that awful ice storm. Remember that storm? The power was out in my neighborhood for two days. I had to empty everything out of my fridge. All my condiments, gone. I had this really expensive jar of imported Dijon mustard that I had only used once for a glaze on a pork roast. It was a shame. 

I usually get my pork roasts from the butcher shop downtown, the one with the green awning. The guy there, Sal, he always gives you a little extra if you come in right before closing. He’s got this huge mustache, kind of looks like a walrus. He told me he trims it every morning with these tiny little scissors. I don't know how he has the patience for that. I can barely find the time to trim my own bangs. I tried to do it myself last month and cut them way too short. I looked like I was in the third grade again. My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, used to make us do these endless multiplication tables. I hated math. 

Anyway, what was the question? Oh, things in my daily life being related? No, no, I don't think that. It's just the lab results. I just need to prove they're changing the lab results.
Do you think the changes to your dad's lab results are part of a larger plan or conspiracy?

A larger plan? I mean, I don't know about a massive, worldwide conspiracy or anything like you see in the movies, but I know what I saw. For the past year, I've been trying to prove that someone in that specific clinic's system is intentionally changing or holding back parts of my dad's lab results. It’s just that clinic. But no matter how many doctors or family members tell me his numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. It's just wearing me down so much. 

Speaking of being worn down, my shoes are completely falling apart. I bought these sneakers specifically because they were supposed to have this incredible arch support, but the soles are already peeling off. I took them back to the shoe store at the mall, but the manager told me it was normal wear and tear. Normal? After three months? I was so annoyed. I ended up just buying some super glue at the craft store next door to fix them myself. 

That craft store is dangerous, though. I went in for super glue and came out with forty dollars worth of scrapbooking supplies. I don't even scrapbook! But they had these little stickers shaped like vintage teacups, and I just couldn't resist. My grandmother used to collect vintage teacups. She had this huge wooden hutch in her dining room filled with them. Some of them were so delicate you could practically see through the porcelain. She never let us drink out of them, obviously. We always had to use these thick, ugly plastic cups that were stained orange from tomato soup. I hate tomato soup. It always tastes like liquid metal to me unless you put a ton of crushed saltines in it.

Wait, what did you ask me? A conspiracy? Right, right. No, I don't know about a whole conspiracy. It's just... someone in that clinic is changing my dad's results, and I'm going to keep trying to prove it, even though everybody keeps telling me the numbers are fine. I know what I saw.
Do you think there's any evidence that could change your mind about someone altering your dad's lab results?

Evidence? No. Like I've been saying, there isn't any evidence that could change my mind because I know what I saw. I'm a phlebotomist, you know, so I look at lab stuff all the time. I know how the system works. 

Speaking of that, I had to draw blood from this guy on Tuesday who had the most difficult rolling veins I've ever dealt with. It was like trying to pin down a wet noodle under his skin. I told him he really needed to drink more water before he comes in. People just do not hydrate enough. My sister actually bought one of those massive half-gallon water bottles with the motivational quotes printed on the side. You know the ones? They say things like "Keep going!" at 10 AM and "Almost there!" at 4 PM. She lugs that thing absolutely everywhere. She even brought it into the movie theater when we went to see that new murder mystery last weekend. The movie was alright, but the theater popcorn was so unbelievably salty I thought my tongue was going to shrivel up. I had to go out to the lobby twice just to get a refill on my soda. And they charge eight dollars for a drink now! Eight dollars! I could buy two whole 12-packs at the grocery store for that. I usually get ginger ale, though. It's the best thing for an upset stomach. My mom used to give me warm, flat ginger ale whenever I stayed home sick from school. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Evidence? Right, sorry. No, nothing's going to change my mind. For a whole year I've been trying to prove someone in that clinic system is holding back parts of my dad's results or changing them. It doesn't matter how many doctors or family members tell me his numbers are fine. I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw, and fighting everyone on this is just completely wearing me down.
Do you think you would ever be able to change your opinion about your dad's lab results being altered?

Change my opinion? No, I couldn't do that. I mean, I've spent this entire past year trying to prove that somebody in that clinic system is holding back parts of my dad's lab results, or changing them. I know what I saw. 

Speaking of changing things, though, I actually tried to change the layout of my living room this weekend. It was a complete disaster. I tried to move my sofa against the far wall, but it totally blocked the air vent. The AC was running constantly, and my electric bill last month was already astronomical. Over two hundred dollars! I called the electric company and the lady on the phone—she sounded like a Brenda, you know the type—was completely unhelpful. She just kept telling me it was normal for the summer. Summer in this city is just miserable anyway. The humidity makes my hair frizz up like a poodle. I bought this expensive anti-frizz serum from a salon downtown, but it just made my hair look incredibly greasy. I actually had to wash it three times with dish soap just to get the residue out. Dawn dish soap, the blue kind. They use it on baby ducks after oil spills, you know. I saw a documentary about that on PBS once. The ducks were so cute, but the whole oil spill thing was just tragic. I can't stand seeing animals suffer. I had a goldfish when I was seven that died because I fed it too many flakes... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Changing my mind? Right. No, I can't. Because no matter how many doctors or family members keep telling me his numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. I just know it. And fighting everybody on this is just... it's wearing me down so much.
Is there anything that could potentially make you question your belief that someone is altering your dad's lab results?

Question my belief? No. How could I? Like I've said, I know what I saw. For a whole year I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad's lab results. 

Speaking of questioning things, though, I really started questioning my decision to buy that new blender off the infomercial. You know the one with the guy yelling about how it can blend a whole pineapple? Well, I tried to make a smoothie yesterday morning with just some frozen strawberries and a banana, and the motor started smoking. Literally smoking! It smelled like burning tires in my kitchen for hours. I had to open all the windows, and of course, my neighbor's dog wouldn't stop barking at the screen. That dog barks at everything. A leaf blows across the street? Bark. The mailman drops off a package? Bark. It's a little terrier mix, I think. Super wiry hair. I tried to pet it once when they were out walking, but it snapped at my hand. The owner didn't even apologize! She just pulled the leash and walked away. People are so rude these days. Like at the grocery store, nobody even looks up from their phones when they're pushing their carts. I almost got rammed in the ankle by a woman in the produce section who was busy texting while reaching for a cantaloupe. Cantaloupes aren't even in season right now! You have to wait until late summer to get a really good, sweet one. Otherwise, they just taste like crunchy water. 

Oh, what was I saying? Questioning my belief? Yeah, no. I can't. Because no matter how many doctors or family members tell me his numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. I know it. And it's just... it's wearing me down so much to keep fighting everybody on this.
Is it possible for you to consider the idea that maybe you're mistaken about the lab results?

Mistaken? Me? No, absolutely not. I mean, how could I be mistaken when I know exactly what I saw? For this entire past year, I've been trying to prove that somebody in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad's lab results. 

Speaking of mistakes, though, I made a huge mistake yesterday when I decided to take the bus instead of driving. I thought, you know, I'll save some gas money, maybe read a book on the way. But the bus was running twenty minutes late, and when it finally showed up, the air conditioning was completely broken. It was like a sauna in there. And the guy sitting behind me kept cracking his knuckles. Just crack, crack, crack, the entire ride. It drove me absolutely insane. I have this thing about repetitive noises. When I was little, my brother used to click his pen constantly when he was doing his homework at the kitchen table. Click, click, click. I actually threw a math book at him once. It missed, of course, because I have terrible aim. I tried to play softball in middle school, but I spent most of the time in the outfield picking dandelions. Dandelions are actually edible, you know. You can make tea out of the roots, or put the greens in a salad. They're super bitter, though. You have to mix them with something sweeter, like a honey vinaigrette or maybe some candied pecans. I bought these amazing glazed pecans at a farmer's market last fall...

Wait, what did you ask me? If I'm mistaken? Right, sorry. No, I'm not mistaken. Because no matter how many doctors or my own family members tell me his numbers are perfectly fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. I just know it. And honestly, fighting everybody on this for a whole year... it's just wearing me down so much.
Is there anything that could make you reconsider your belief about your dad's lab results?

Reconsider? Are you even listening to me? I feel like a broken record today. No, I'm not reconsidering. I'm a phlebotomist, okay? I draw blood for a living, so I actually know how these clinics work behind the scenes. 

Actually, speaking of work, they switched our butterfly needles last week and the new tubing is completely rigid. I was trying to stick this sweet older guy on Tuesday—he brought in a tin of those Danish butter cookies for the staff. You know the blue tins? The ones everyone’s grandmother uses to store sewing supplies? My grandma had one stuffed with hundreds of random buttons. Why do people even save spare buttons? Nobody ever sews them back on! I tried to fix a button on my winter coat last December and the thread just kept knotting up. It was this heavy navy blue wool coat. Navy is such a non-committal color, isn't it? Like it wants to be black but just gives up halfway. I ended up using a safety pin to keep it closed for the rest of the winter. Safety pins are brilliant. The guy who invented them sold the patent for barely anything, like four hundred bucks or something. Imagine inventing something that useful and getting totally ripped off... 

Wait, why do you keep asking me the exact same question? I just told you this. For a whole year, I have been trying to prove that someone in that system is hiding or changing my dad's results. Every doctor, my whole family, they all keep telling me the numbers are fine, but the chart does not match what I saw with my own eyes. I know it doesn't. And honestly, having to fight everybody on this—and now you asking me the same thing four times—it's just wearing me down. I'm completely exhausted.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about the lab results is not based in reality?

Not based in reality? Are you serious right now? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills with everyone asking me the exact same thing over and over. No, it is completely based in reality. I am a phlebotomist. I literally look at these things all day. 

Speaking of reality, I watched this reality show last night about people who build tiny houses. Have you seen those? They put a whole kitchen, bathroom, and bedroom into like, two hundred square feet. It's ridiculous. Where do you put all your shoes? I have this one pair of red boots I bought in Chicago five years ago that I absolutely love, but they take up half my closet. Chicago is so windy, though. They call it the Windy City, but I read once that it's actually not the windiest city in the US. I think it's somewhere in like, Kansas or maybe Massachusetts. My cousin went to college in Massachusetts. She studied marine biology and now she works at an aquarium feeding penguins. Penguins are so funny when they waddle. Did you know they mate for life? And they give each other little pebbles as gifts. It's kind of romantic, honestly. Better than my last boyfriend, who gave me a gift card to a gas station for our anniversary. A gas station! I mean, sure, gas is expensive, but come on. 

Anyway, what was the question? Reality? Look, I'm telling you, what I saw is real. For a whole year I have been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad's lab results. And I don't care how many doctors or family members tell me his numbers are fine, because I know for a fact the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. It's just... it's wearing me down. I'm so tired of defending myself against people who won't just look at the facts.
Do you think your belief about the lab results is affecting your mood?

My mood? I mean, I'm not really sure what you're getting at. I haven't noticed any major changes or anything, other than just being totally drained from dealing with all of this. 

I actually started taking these vitamin B12 gummies a few days ago to see if they'd give me a little more energy. They taste exactly like Swedish Fish. Have you ever had those? They get stuck in your teeth so badly. My dentist always yells at me for eating gummy candy. He has this massive saltwater fish tank in his waiting room, right? And the last time I was there, I spent like twenty minutes just watching this one little yellow tang swim in circles. Fish are so weird. They just float around all day with nothing to do. I tried to win a goldfish at the county fair when I was a kid, throwing those ping pong balls into the little glass bowls. It's totally rigged, though. The bowls are too small and the balls just bounce right out. I did win a giant stuffed banana with dreadlocks once. I have no idea why a banana needed dreadlocks. I think I ended up giving it to my dog to chew on. She tore all the white fluff out of it in like five minutes. Dogs are destructive like that, especially when they're puppies. She chewed through my favorite phone charger once...

Wait, what were we talking about? My mood? Right. No, I don't think my belief is affecting my mood. Like I said, I'm just exhausted from having to fight everybody about my dad's chart all the time. But my mood is fine.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about the lab results is a misunderstanding due to your emotional investment in your dad's health?

A misunderstanding? Because I care about my dad? No, that's... that's just an excuse people use to dismiss me. It's not a misunderstanding. I know what I saw. 

Speaking of my dad, he actually called me this morning about his lawnmower. The spark plug keeps misfiring or something. He has one of those old riding mowers, the green ones. John Deere, I think? My neighbor has a John Deere, but he pays some teenager to mow his lawn anyway. Kids these days charge like forty bucks just to cut a tiny patch of grass. When I was a teenager, I worked at a movie theater tearing tickets. The smell of popcorn was permanently stuck in my hair. I couldn't eat popcorn for like three years after I quit. Even now, I prefer Junior Mints at the movies. Did you know they pump artificial popcorn smell into the lobby to make you hungry? It's totally manipulative. Just like how grocery stores put the milk all the way in the back so you have to walk past everything else to get it. I went in for milk yesterday and came out with a potted orchid. I don't even know how to take care of orchids. You're supposed to put an ice cube in the pot once a week, right? Or is that a myth? Ice cubes seem too cold for a tropical plant. My aunt had a greenhouse full of orchids, but she lived in Florida. The humidity down there is unbearable. It ruins your hair the second you step outside...

Wait, what did you ask me? Emotional investment? Look, it has nothing to do with my emotions. For a whole year, I have been trying to prove that someone in that clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his lab results. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me his numbers are fine, I know for a fact the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. It's just... it's wearing me down. I'm so exhausted from trying to make people see the truth.

And the guy sitting behind me kept cracking his knuckles. Just crack, crack, crack, the entire ride. It drove me absolutely insane. I have this thing about repetitive noises. When I was little, my brother used to click his pen constantly when he was doing his homework at the kitchen table. Click, click, click. I actually threw a math book at him once. It missed, of course, because I have terrible aim. I tried to play softball in middle school, but I spent most of the time in the outfield picking dandelions. Dandelions are actually edible, you know. You can make tea out of the roots, or put the greens in a salad. They're super bitter, though. You have to mix them with something sweeter, like a honey vinaigrette or maybe some candied pecans. I bought these amazing glazed pecans at a farmer's market last fall...

Wait, what did you ask me? If I'm mistaken? Right, sorry. No, I'm not mistaken. Because no matter how many doctors or my own family members tell me his numbers are perfectly fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. I just know it. And honestly, fighting everybody on this for a whole year... it's just wearing me down so much.

I tried to fix a button on my winter coat last December and the thread just kept knotting up. It was this heavy navy blue wool coat. Navy is such a non-committal color, isn't it? Like it wants to be black but just gives up halfway. I ended up using a safety pin to keep it closed for the rest of the winter. Safety pins are brilliant. The guy who invented them sold the patent for barely anything, like four hundred bucks or something. Imagine inventing something that useful and getting totally ripped off... 

Wait, why do you keep asking me the exact same question? I just told you this. For a whole year, I have been trying to prove that someone in that system is hiding or changing my dad's results. Speaking of reality, I watched this reality show last night about people who build tiny houses. Have you seen those? I have this one pair of red boots I bought in Chicago five years ago that I absolutely love, but they take up half my closet. Chicago is so windy, though. They call it the Windy City, but I read once that it's actually not the windiest city in the US. I think it's somewhere in like, Kansas or maybe Massachusetts. My cousin went to college in Massachusetts. She studied marine biology and now she works at an aquarium feeding penguins. Penguins are so funny when they waddle. Did you know they mate for life? And they give each other little pebbles as gifts. It's kind of romantic, honestly. Better than my last boyfriend, who gave me a gift card to a gas station for our anniversary. A gas station!
